archetype: small suburban cul-de-sac cluster with several distinct detached homes, shared turning bulb, driveways, utility edge and neglected communal streetscape
ground_program: single feeder road entering a widened turning bulb sized for ordinary residential vehicle circulation rather than a decorative circular plaza
five detached residential lots arranged around the bulb with individually oriented front doors, driveways and setbacks
each house receives a distinct ground-floor domestic arrangement using living, kitchen/dining, utility and circulation modules without becoming a renamed clone
at least three attached or detached garages distributed across the lots with full driveway connections to the street
side-yard and rear-yard access paths preserving clear lot boundaries and service circulation
mailbox or shared delivery point near the feeder-road entrance without blocking the roadway
storm-drain, curb or ditch treatment following the bulb and feeder road so runoff has a coherent downhill route
street lighting and utility distribution following the road edge with service drops or connections to individual lots
small neglected play or sitting area on one widened verge to establish community use without replacing residential lots
front walks connecting every surviving principal entrance to its driveway or street edge
terrain feathering that preserves individual lot grades instead of placing the entire neighborhood on one flat platform
upper_program: a mix of single-storey and two-storey or raised-roof houses so the street silhouette varies across the cluster
upper bedroom and bathroom zones only where supported by a coherent stair and lower-floor circulation core
roof forms vary by house footprint while remaining structurally supported by surviving exterior and interior walls
no disconnected decorative upper rooms or inaccessible attic boxes
circulation: vehicles enter from the feeder road, circulate around the bulb and can reach each driveway without crossing private yards
pedestrians can move from every principal entrance to the street and between neighboring frontages without walking through garages
each multi-storey dwelling uses a supported stair with real landings, continuous headroom and a destination on both ends
rear and side service routes remain lot-specific rather than forming an implausible continuous alley unless the terrain explicitly supports one
utility and drainage routes follow the public edge or lot boundaries and do not cut through primary rooms
damage_constraints: preserve the feeder road, turning bulb and at least three recognizable residential lots so the scene remains a cul-de-sac rather than isolated house ruins
vary damage severity and mechanism by lot: one partial roof failure, one facade/garage impact, one fire-damaged interior, and lighter abandonment elsewhere
do not apply identical missing-wall masks, rubble patterns or roof failures across multiple houses
keep at least one fully navigable house and several partially navigable homes to preserve neighborhood-scale exploration
allow localized pavement cracking, vegetation intrusion and curb failure without erasing the underlying road geometry
damage doors, windows, stairs, roofs, fences and utility attachments together with their supporting structure so no floating fragments remain
retain enough domestic furnishing and lot-specific service evidence that each surviving dwelling reads as a home rather than an empty shell
preserve credible foundation and driveway contact at all surviving buildings
derive damaged and occupied variants only from this immutable clean master

required_manual_checks: the complete site reads immediately as a residential cul-de-sac with a functional turning bulb and distinct private lots
individual houses differ in footprint, roofline, circulation and damage story rather than appearing as rotated clones
roads, driveways, front walks and lot access are player-scale usable and meet terrain without severe steps or floating slabs
multi-storey houses have supported stairs, sufficient headroom and real landings at both ends
utility, drainage and streetscape elements reinforce the neighborhood layout without obstructing circulation
damage varies coherently across the cluster while preserving at least three recognizable homes and the street plan
the site transitions into surrounding wasteland terrain without a monolithic rectangular foundation or artificial neighborhood platform
